explanation: The statement is about the library-only definition `HomologicalComplex.cyclesShortComplex` (the short complex `Zᵢ -iCycles-> Kᵢ -toCycles-> Zⱼ`), which does not exist in Mathlib (grep for `cyclesShortComplex` over the whole Mathlib tree gives no hits). Mathlib's closest facts are `HomologicalComplex.cyclesIsKernel` (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/HomologicalComplex.lean, line 136), which says `K.iCycles i` is a kernel of the *differential* `K.d i j : K.X i ⟶ K.X j`, not of the corestricted map `K.toCycles i j : K.X i ⟶ K.cycles j`, together with the generic criteria `ShortComplex.exact_of_f_is_kernel`, `ShortComplex.exact_iff_iCycles_pOpcycles_zero` and `ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono`. Getting exactness of the cycles sequence from any single one of these requires either providing an `IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (K.iCycles i) _)` for `K.toCycles i j` (via `isKernelOfComp` with the monomorphism `K.iCycles j`, as the library proof does) or constructing an explicit morphism of short complexes between the cycles sequence and `ShortComplex.mk (K.iCycles i) (K.d i j) _` and applying `exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono`; either way the derivation is more than one or two lines and combines several Mathlib results with an auxiliary construction. I also checked Mathlib's HomologySequence.lean (`cycles_left_exact`, `opcycles_right_exact`, `composableArrows₃_exact`), the SpectralObject files (`kernelSequenceOpcycles_exact`, etc.), and Abelian.lean for any statement of the form `K.iCycles i` being a kernel of `K.toCycles i j` or of exactness of `Zᵢ ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ`; none exists.
